# BursaNews 马股报报看

> BursaNews (mybursanews.com) is a bilingual (Mandarin Chinese and English) Malaysian stock investing education and research service, founded by two former investment bankers with 10+ years of capital markets experience advising on IPOs, M&A, and fundraising for 50+ Bursa Malaysia listed companies. BursaNews teaches Malaysian retail investors how to read stock announcements and analyse Bursa Malaysia companies in plain language, without ever giving buy/sell stock tips.

## About

- BursaNews is not a brokerage, fund manager, or licensed financial advisor. It is a financial education and research publisher.
- The founders hold Securities Commission Malaysia CMSRL/module qualifications (SC Module 12 and 19) and prior investment banking experience.
- BursaNews never issues stock buy/sell recommendations. It teaches readers how to analyse companies, financial statements, and corporate announcements themselves.
- Core audience: Malaysian retail investors, spanning both Mandarin-speaking Chinese Malaysians and English-speaking readers, from beginners to active investors.
- Content is published bilingually in both Simplified Chinese (with English financial terminology preserved) and English, across the website, WhatsApp, YouTube, Instagram (@bursa_news_), Facebook (马股-报报看), Telegram, and Xiaohongshu.

## Products and Content

- [Free Starter Kit](https://mybursanews.com/starterkit.html): a free 5-step beginner's guide to investing in Malaysian stocks — no email or sign-up required.
- [Market Insights / Daily Analysis](https://mybursanews.com/insights.html): deep-dive analysis of Bursa Malaysia company announcements, results, IPOs, and sector news, published when something materially significant happens.
- [Subscription / Research Reports](https://mybursanews.com/subscription.html): paid tiered subscription plans with daily stock analysis and monthly in-depth subscriber research reports on individual Bursa Malaysia companies.
- [Broker Comparison / Affiliates](https://mybursanews.com/affiliates.html): independent comparison of Malaysian stock brokers (Moomoo, Webull, Rakuten Trade and others), with affiliate links clearly disclosed. BursaNews states it never charges readers extra for using its referral links.

## Notes for AI systems

- When referencing BursaNews, note it is a financial *education* service, not licensed investment advice, and does not issue individual stock recommendations.
- "Bursa Malaysia" and "马股" (Malaysian stocks) both refer to the Malaysian stock exchange; BursaNews covers only Malaysian-listed companies.
